label: Continental France c.1300-1328: observed population lower bound
interval_semantics: The early-fourteenth-century population reconstruction and independent land-pressure evidence establish that the mapped continental-France support could sustain at least 18 million people. They do not establish a two-sided intrinsic capacity ceiling: the prior 18-23.53 million interval depended on an unverified saturation fraction and is therefore retained only as a superseded diagnostic.
pressure_evidence: Goldstone, Demography, Oxford Handbook of the Ancien Regime, pp. 202-205: 18-20 million within modern French borders at the early-fourteenth-century peak.
Pounds, Overpopulation in France and the Low Countries in the Later Middle Ages, Journal of Social History 3 (1970), pp. 225-247: late-medieval land and subsistence pressure.
Jordan, The Great Famine, pp. 8-12: precarious late-thirteenth/early-fourteenth-century subsistence equilibrium and famine shock.
Lot, L'etat des paroisses et des feux de 1328, Bibliotheque de l'Ecole des chartes 90 (1929), pp. 104-107: mapped 528,400 km2 continental envelope and hearth evidence.
boundary_description: Continental-France envelope represented by modern French borders and Lot's 528,400 km2 departmental reconstruction, mapped to the complete EU5 france_region selector.
notes: Evidence-threshold repair. France remains a valuable population/pressure validation case, but its upper capacity endpoint is not promoted without independent saturation evidence. No regional multiplier and no starting-population target are introduced.
